lesson_title: Inflation and the CPI: One Trolley, Priced Twice
hook_text: One number moves your rent, your grant, your bond and the price of bread. Here's the trolley it comes from.
clip_script: Every month, one number moves the repo rate, wage talks, grants and rent. Where does it come from? A trolley. Statistics South Africa asked thousands of households what they buy — mielie meal, taxi fare, electricity, airtime, a funeral policy — and built ONE trolley that stands for the whole country. Housing takes the biggest corner. Food takes a big one. Then price collectors price that SAME trolley, month after month. Base year: the trolley costs R4 000 — call it 100. Two years later: R4 480. Divide, times 100 — the marker reads 112. That's the CPI. Now the news number: last year the marker said 112, this year 118,7. It moved 6,7 points — but against the 112 you started from, that's a 6 percent journey. THAT is the inflation rate. Not guessed. Not felt. One trolley, priced twice, compared. And here's why your family swears prices rose faster: your trolley isn't the country's trolley. Spend half your money on food, and food inflation hits you double-strength. Both numbers are true — one is an average, and nobody is average.
visual_style: A single shopping trolley rolling through a month-by-month calendar, items stacking with different sizes for their weights; a price tag flipping from R4 000 to R4 480; a speedometer needle sweeping from 112 to 118,7 and printing 6,0%.
pacing: Steady build through the trolley, a snap at the divide-and-compare move, warm landing on the average-versus-you twist.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and calculate any inflation rate — and know who wins and loses when prices run.
